evidence.title: Renewable Energy-Based Hybrid Power Conversion System for Induction Motor Driven Light Electric Vehicle
evidence.abstract: This paper validates a solar photovoltaic (SPV) based induction motor (IM) system using a modified quasi-impedance source inverter (qZSI) for electric vehicles. The system employs a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm to control the Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) output, connected to a modified qZSI. This study covers the design, control, and performance analysis of a powertrain for electric vehicles driven by a battery and solar-fed induction motor. The DC-link modified qZSI converter offers high gain voltage conversion in both charging and discharging modes, interfacing with the low voltage battery. Solar energy is integrated through the modified qZSI, which manages MPPT, maximizes efficiency, and reduces current ripple at the SPV end. The Perturb and Observe (P&O) technique is used to maximise the PV panel's power output. The induction motor operates in open-loop mode, and active power flow is controlled via DC-link voltage regulation. This setup generates an AC voltage higher than the DC input based on the instantaneous duty cycle, unlike traditional VSI systems. The proposed system uses a three-phase hybrid qZSI converter to power an induction motor drive, which is isolated with an isolation transformer for safety. The qZSI boosts the DC voltage of the solar array, with switches controlled by Pulse Width Modulation and shoot-through signals from the MPPT connected to the SPV. Benefits include fewer required switches and improved output voltage quality, and efficiency, enabling a variable frequency induction motor drive and extending the driving range. Detailed analysis, including mathematical expressions and real-time simulations, has been conducted using the Typhoon HIL 402 real-time emulator.

cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

First, the artificial potential field guidance method is applied to engine management, integrating the engine's knock risk and thermal efficiency into the design of the dedicated field. Then, a Bees-inspired adaptive optimisation method is combined with a typical series-parallel state machine to split the required power for different power sources. custody_records.raw_content: This paper validates a solar photovoltaic (SPV) based induction motor (IM) system using a modified quasi-impedance source inverter (qZSI) for electric vehicles. The system employs a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm to control the Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) output, connected to a modified qZSI. This study covers the design, control, and performance analysis of a powertrain for electric vehicles driven by a battery and solar-fed induction motor. The DC-link modified qZSI converter offers high gain voltage conversion in both charging and discharging modes, interfacing with the low voltage battery. Solar energy is integrated through the modified qZSI, which manages MPPT, maximizes efficiency, and reduces current ripple at the SPV end. The Perturb and Observe (P&O) technique is used to maximise the PV panel's power output. The induction motor operates in open-loop mode, and active power flow is controlled via DC-link voltage regulation. This setup generates an AC voltage higher than the DC input based on the instantaneous duty cycle, unlike traditional VSI systems. The proposed system uses a three-phase hybrid qZSI converter to power an induction motor drive, which is isolated with an isolation transformer for safety. The qZSI boosts the DC voltage of the solar array, with switches controlled by Pulse Width Modulation and shoot-through signals from the MPPT connected to the SPV. Benefits include fewer required switches and improved output voltage quality, and efficiency, enabling a variable frequency induction motor drive and extending the driving range. Detailed analysis, including mathematical expressions and real-time simulations, has been conducted using the Typhoon HIL 402 real-time emulator.
